sn12.21:1.2: “Bhikkhus, possessing the ten powers and the four grounds of self-confidence, the Tathagata claims the place of the chief bull of the herd, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the Brahma-wheel thus:
sn12.21:1.3: ‘Such is form, such its origin, such its passing away;
sn12.21:1.4: such is feeling, such its origin, such its passing away;
sn12.21:1.5: such is perception, such its origin, such its passing away;
sn12.21:1.6: such are volitional formations, such their origin, such their passing away;
sn12.21:1.7: such is consciousness, such its origin, such its passing away.
sn12.21:1.8: Thus when this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises.
sn12.21:1.9: When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.
sn12.21:1.10: That is, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.21:1.11: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….
sn12.21:1.12: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.21:1.13: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations; with the cessation of volitional formations,
sn12.21:1.15: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’”
